evidence.claim: Buhari said the redesigned naira would help address illicit financial flows, corruption, the economy, and the value of the currency, while the CBN said the policy would help control money supply and support monetary policy.
evidence.title: Buhari unveils redesigned naira notes
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said the redesigned naira would help address illicit financial flows, corruption, the economy, and the value of the currency, while the CBN said the policy would help control money supply and support monetary policy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a formal policy unveiling with direct quotes from Buhari and Emefiele.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari and CBN policy intent.
contrary_evidence: The policy later triggered cash-scarcity problems
intent to fight corruption does not prove effective implementation

evidence.claim: Buhari said the 2022 budget was guided by 2021-2025 National Development Plan objectives including diversification, infrastructure, security, a vibrant educated and healthy populace, reducing poverty, and minimizing regional, economic, and social disparities, and he described it as intended to improve the living conditions of Nigerians.
evidence.title: 2022 Budget Speech: Budget of Economic Growth and Sustainability – President Buhari
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said the 2022 budget was guided by 2021-2025 National Development Plan objectives including diversification, infrastructure, security, a vibrant educated and healthy populace, reducing poverty, and minimizing regional, economic, and social disparities, and he described it as intended to improve the living conditions of Nigerians.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential budget speech during the target year, with explicit welfare-oriented objectives and strong ruler attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 budget speech in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari statement as president; strong attribution to executive intent, though not proof of implementation.
contrary_evidence: The speech is aspirational and does not by itself prove delivered welfare gains.
Nigeria still had severe poverty and human-development gaps in 2022.

evidence.claim: The Ministry of Health said the federal government had released N89 billion to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund, disbursed N56 billion to all 36 states and the FCT, and was providing operational funds to 7,250 primary health care facilities in 35 states and the FCT, aiming for at least one functional PHC in every ward.
evidence.title: BHCPF: FG DISBURSES N56 BILLION TO 36 STATES, FCT
evidence.publisher: Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Health said the federal government had released N89 billion to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund, disbursed N56 billion to all 36 states and the FCT, and was providing operational funds to 7,250 primary health care facilities in 35 states and the FCT, aiming for at least one functional PHC in every ward.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry report with concrete disbursement and facility figures, but still an executive-side report rather than an audit.
evidence.period_fit: August 2022 target-period reporting on ongoing 2022 delivery.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Federal health-finance attribution is strong, though actual service delivery depended on state and facility execution.
contrary_evidence: Disbursement does not guarantee quality or access at point of care.
The release does not show whether all wards received functional PHCs.

evidence.claim: Buhari appointed Dr Doyin Salami chief economic adviser and defined the role around monitoring domestic and international developments and recommending macroeconomic policy responses for stability, growth, jobs, and poverty reduction.
evidence.title: President Buhari Appoints Dr Doyin Salami as Chief Economic Adviser
evidence.excerpt: Buhari appointed Dr Doyin Salami chief economic adviser and defined the role around monitoring domestic and international developments and recommending macroeconomic policy responses for stability, growth, jobs, and poverty reduction.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government notice of the appointment and duties; the appointment fact is direct and specific.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari appointment under his executive authority; effectiveness still depended on the adviser and the wider economic team.
contrary_evidence: The later 2022 macro record still showed high inflation, subsidy pressure, and weak revenue performance.

evidence.claim: Buhari launched the National Development Plan 2021-2025, set targets of about 5 percent average real GDP growth, 21 million jobs, and 35 million people lifted from poverty, and said a Vice-President-led implementation unit would coordinate delivery across ministries and stakeholders.
evidence.title: President Buhari: Nigeria Needs N348.1tr Investments to Achieve 5-Year National Development Plan
evidence.excerpt: Buhari launched the National Development Plan 2021-2025, set targets of about 5 percent average real GDP growth, 21 million jobs, and 35 million people lifted from poverty, and said a Vice-President-led implementation unit would coordinate delivery across ministries and stakeholders.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary launch speech with clear targets, financing assumptions, and implementation architecture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari launch and ownership of the plan; execution depended on ministries, subnational actors, and private-sector financing.
contrary_evidence: The plan’s target setting was more explicit than the evidence of full realization by end-2022.

evidence.claim: Buhari inaugurated a Presidential Committee on the Economy that brought together senior economic officials, including the vice president, finance minister, CBN governor, governors forum leadership, and the chief economic adviser, to act as a rapid-response economic coordination mechanism.
evidence.title: Despite Strong Headwings, Nigeria’s Economy Continues to Grow- President Buhari
evidence.excerpt: Buhari inaugurated a Presidential Committee on the Economy that brought together senior economic officials, including the vice president, finance minister, CBN governor, governors forum leadership, and the chief economic adviser, to act as a rapid-response economic coordination mechanism.
evidence.source_locator: body paragraphs describing the committee and its mandate
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government account of the committee’s creation, membership, and purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari-chaired initiative; the committee sat within his executive authority, though delivery still depended on cooperating institutions.
contrary_evidence: Later macro reports still found that major fiscal and monetary problems were not solved.

evidence.claim: At the NIFF launch, Buhari said inclusive and broad-based development was a cardinal administration objective and said the financing framework was designed to map a sustainable financing plan for the SDGs and Nigeria’s development plans.
evidence.title: At Launch Of Integrated Financing System, President Buhari Restates Nigeria’s Commitment To Achieving Sustainable Development Goals
evidence.excerpt: At the NIFF launch, Buhari said inclusive and broad-based development was a cardinal administration objective and said the financing framework was designed to map a sustainable financing plan for the SDGs and Nigeria’s development plans.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary launch speech with explicit implementation and financing language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari policy ownership, though the framework’s effectiveness depended on the finance ministry, agencies, and partners.
contrary_evidence: The existence of the framework did not itself prove faster delivery by year-end.

evidence.claim: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill into law and said it would create a fund to cover 83 million poor Nigerians, work with state schemes, and use information systems for data collection, monitoring, and quality assurance.
evidence.title: In Bid to Achieve Universal Coverage, President Buhari Signs National Health Authority Bill Into Law
evidence.excerpt: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill into law and said it would create a fund to cover 83 million poor Nigerians, work with state schemes, and use information systems for data collection, monitoring, and quality assurance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary record of a law, the intended beneficiary group, and the implementation pathway.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari assent to the law; implementation then depended on the health bureaucracy and states.
contrary_evidence: The law’s passage did not by itself establish full coverage by end-2022.

evidence.claim: Nigeria’s NPHCDA, with WHO and partner support, integrated COVID-19 vaccination with routine immunization and vitamin A supplementation, and began zero-dose reduction planning in selected states.
evidence.title: States adopt integrated vaccination strategy to reach unimmunized children
evidence.excerpt: Nigeria’s NPHCDA, with WHO and partner support, integrated COVID-19 vaccination with routine immunization and vitamin A supplementation, and began zero-dose reduction planning in selected states.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral reporting on a concrete delivery change and rollout in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The initiative ran through Nigeria’s federal PHC apparatus under Buhari’s administration, though delivery was shared with states and partners.
contrary_evidence: Coverage gaps remained large, so the rollout was partial rather than universal.

evidence.claim: Nigeria, through the National Primary Health Care Development Agency with WHO support, introduced the rotavirus vaccine into routine immunization in 2022, with the stated goal of preventing more than 50,000 child deaths annually.
evidence.title: Nigeria to avert 50,000 deaths in children annually, introduces rotavirus vaccine into vaccination schedule
evidence.excerpt: Nigeria, through the National Primary Health Care Development Agency with WHO support, introduced the rotavirus vaccine into routine immunization in 2022, with the stated goal of preventing more than 50,000 child deaths annually.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral source describing a discrete implementation event and intended outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Implemented through Buhari’s federal health system, though subnational delivery and partner support were essential.
contrary_evidence: The need to introduce the vaccine underscores that baseline child-health outcomes were still weak.

evidence.claim: The federal government launched the 2022 Multidimensional Poverty Index survey as a nationwide, subnationally disaggregated data tool to inform evidence-based policy, budgeting, and resource allocation.
evidence.title: Nigeria Launches its Most Extensive National Measure of Multidimensional Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The federal government launched the 2022 Multidimensional Poverty Index survey as a nationwide, subnationally disaggregated data tool to inform evidence-based policy, budgeting, and resource allocation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary statistics agency release describing a concrete measurement and budgeting tool.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The survey was produced under Buhari’s government, but the data tool was a shared federal-statistical effort with development partners.
contrary_evidence: The report also exposed the scale of persistent poverty rather than showing that it had already been solved.

evidence.claim: The IMF said higher oil prices created an opportunity to build fiscal space and FX reserves but the opportunity was not harnessed; inflation was elevated, fuel subsidies remained a major fiscal drain, and Nigeria needed tighter macro policy, stronger revenue mobilization, exchange-rate reform, and trade and agricultural reforms.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Staff Concluding Statement of the 2022 Article IV Mission
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said higher oil prices created an opportunity to build fiscal space and FX reserves but the opportunity was not harnessed; inflation was elevated, fuel subsidies remained a major fiscal drain, and Nigeria needed tighter macro policy, stronger revenue mobilization, exchange-rate reform, and trade and agricultural reforms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Article IV mission statement with explicit 2022 policy and outcome assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The critique is partly attributable to Buhari’s government because it evaluates policies under his administration, but some pressures were inherited or global.
contrary_evidence: The statement also notes that growth continued and some tax-automation reform was advancing.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said gasoline subsidies would cost about 5 trillion naira in 2022, crowding out spending on infrastructure, education, health, and investment, and recommended coordinated exchange-rate, subsidy, tax, and investment reforms.
evidence.title: A 'Business Unusual' approach, even more urgently needed to reduce inflation, lessen fiscal pressures, and attract investment for jobs
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said gasoline subsidies would cost about 5 trillion naira in 2022, crowding out spending on infrastructure, education, health, and investment, and recommended coordinated exchange-rate, subsidy, tax, and investment reforms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral assessment with specific fiscal estimates and reform priorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The policy burden sat squarely on Buhari’s administration, though global oil prices and inherited structures also mattered.
contrary_evidence: The report is prescriptive and does not by itself prove later implementation success or failure.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the redesigned naira notes were in short supply on the first day of circulation and that many Nigerians said the deadline was too tight, especially in rural and informal markets.
evidence.title: New Nigerian naira notes a rare sight on first day of circulation
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the redesigned naira notes were in short supply on the first day of circulation and that many Nigerians said the deadline was too tight, especially in rural and informal markets.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted witness accounts
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong independent corroboration, though the story focuses on immediate rollout problems rather than the whole policy lifecycle.
evidence.period_fit: direct late-2022 policy rollout and immediate aftermath
evidence.ruler_attribution: The rollout was authorized by Buhari’s administration, but the operational bottlenecks involved CBN and banking channels as well.
contrary_evidence: The report concerns disruption, not a full evaluation of the policy’s intended anti-counterfeiting or cashless objectives.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 ruler-attributed existential-risk choice under Buhari's own authority
Independent corroboration of the HEU-to-LEU conversion and other nuclear-security claims
Independent evidence of actual conflict-management effect from Buhari's Ukraine/ECOWAS diplomacy
Direct documentary support for the contested Lake Chad weapons claim or any concrete cross-border security outcome
More precise chain-of-command and federal-versus-state attribution for abuses and remedies
More direct evidence on Buhari's personal role in media and protest restrictions, beyond security-service and state-level actions
Independent implementation evidence for the 2022 Electoral Act and related reforms
More household-level and distributional evidence on the effects of subsidy, naira redesign, and fiscal choices
Cleaner evidence on whether economic appointees were selected for competence versus loyalty
Independent outcome evaluation of school feeding, BHCPF, rotavirus rollout, and related social programs
Subnational delivery and attribution, especially for north-south and rural-urban differences
Direct evidence on assets, beneficial ownership, gifts, campaign finance, or family enrichment
More independent evidence on truthfulness, correction, and acceptance of scrutiny
Better separation of Buhari's personal conduct from broader authoritarian or state-level behavior
Audited completion data for major projects and service-delivery claims
Independent evidence that coordination bodies and new appointments changed implementation quality
